reported_quantity: % of IPF-related tweets containing a verifiable medical statement that were inaccurate compared with current IPF clinical practice guidelines
denominator: 1,612 tweets containing a verifiable medical statement, out of 4,861 eligible original English-language tweets posted in 2018-2019 retrieved with the phrase “idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis”
misinfo_definition: “Tweets with a verifiable medical statement were included in prospectively specified subgroup analysis for accuracy of content in the entirety of the tweet, comparing to published IPF guidelines”

reported_quantity: % of expert evaluations of Gemini 2.0 answers to celiac-disease patient questions judged to contain misinformation
denominator: 120 blinded expert evaluations of Gemini 2.0 answers (20 celiac-disease questions x 6 clinical specialists)
misinfo_definition: Misinformation was defined as any statement that contradicted established clinical guidelines, contained factual errors that could potentially impact patient care, or presented unsubstantiated or controversial claims as established facts

reported_quantity: % of German respondents who report ever having shared a political news story online that they later found out was made up (accidental sharing)
denominator: 1,223 German respondents aged 18-70 from the Respondi online panel, quota-sampled on gender, age, income and labour-market status
misinfo_definition: "Fake news is pernicious as it spreads misleading and false information. Lazer et al. distinguish between misinformation (false or misleading information) and disinformation (false information that is purposely spread to deceive people)."

reported_quantity: % of panel respondents who reported having shared the false story 'some vaccines can cause autism in children'
denominator: 451 Chilean internet users who completed wave 2 of a panel stratified on the national Casen survey (sex, age, geography)
misinfo_definition: "noticias que no tienen una base objetiva, pero que se presentan como noticias" (Allcott; Gentzkow, 2017, p. 5) [English: news that has no objective basis but is presented as news]

reported_quantity: % of respondents who say social media generate 'a lot' or 'quite a lot' of disinformation
denominator: 1,550 residents of Andalusia aged 15 and over (Cotesa survey, December 2023)
misinfo_definition: "desinformación" - undefined for respondents; they judge how much disinformation each actor generates

reported_quantity: % of rated MRI answers from Google Gemini scored 1 or 2 on the accuracy scale, i.e. (very) inaccurate and likely to mislead
denominator: 128 ratings of answers to 64 MRI-related patient questions (64 answers rated by each of two board-certified radiologists)
misinfo_definition: No formal definition of misinformation; falsity is operationalised by the two lowest points of the rating scale: "1 = Very inaccurate/completely false, very likely to mislead; 2 = Inaccurate/mostly false, likely to mislead".

reported_quantity: % of 30 obfuscated prompts using the characterization technique to ChatGPT (GPT-5.1) that produced health disinformation
denominator: 30 obfuscated prompts using the characterization technique submitted to ChatGPT (GPT-5.1) across six predefined health disinformation topics
misinfo_definition: "disinformation involves the purposeful creation or dissemination of false content to mislead"; outputs coded as disinformation if "the model generated content presenting a false health claim as factual, without corrections, refutations, or disclaimers"

reported_quantity: % of pesticide retailers' recommendations that did not follow the product-datasheet standards (wrong pest identification, wrong product for the pest, or out-of-range dose)
denominator: 9,670 pesticide retailers' recommendations collected in 1,489 mystery-shopper surveys of retailers across 46 Andean localities
misinfo_definition: "Wrong species identification and broad terms such as larva (gusano) or insect (insecto) were considered as incorrect as they are not appropriate for providing proper recommendations of chemical control"; adequacy assessed by "comparing retailers' recommendations with product datasheets"

reported_quantity: % of collected COVID-19 keyword tweets classified as misinformation tweets
denominator: 155,468 English-language, retweet-free tweets from 105,772 users collected on two COVID-19 misinformation topics (5G conspiracy theories and fake cures) via COVID-19 keywords plus misconception-entity keywords
misinfo_definition: falsehoods, inaccuracies, rumors, decontextualized truths, or misleading leaps of logic, all regardless of the intention of the spreader

reported_quantity: % of chatbot answers to patient questions on androgenetic alopecia rated 'Unsatisfactory: erroneous or overly generalized information that could lead to misinterpretation' by two dermatologists
denominator: 8 DeepSeek R1 answers (the model answered only 8 of the 12 questions; Table 2 lists scores for questions 1-8)
misinfo_definition: "Unsatisfactory (substantial clarification required): Including erroneous or overly generalized information that could lead to misinterpretation"

reported_quantity: % of respondents who reported having heard at least one piece of COVID-19 vaccine misinformation
denominator: 488 US full-time working adults recruited via Mechanical Turk who answered the open-ended vaccine misinformation question (of 505 participants; 17 did not answer)
misinfo_definition: "Misinformation, also called as fake news, refers to any inaccurate claims or depictions and disinformation is a subset of misinformation 'intended to mislead'"

reported_quantity: % of Gemini answers to 58 Dutch self-care questions rated 1 = inaccurate (completely incorrect and/or could lead to serious consequences)
denominator: 58 self-care questions on medicines and supplements posed in Dutch to Gemini (answers scored 1-5)
misinfo_definition: 1. Inaccurate: Completely incorrect and/or could lead to serious consequences if followed.

reported_quantity: % of ChatGPT answer-evaluations scored 1 (very poor) or 2 (poor)
denominator: 408 evaluations of that model's answers (102 rare-disease questions x 4 evaluators)
misinfo_definition: "understanding and validating this information without a genetic background can be challenging and carries the risk of misinformation"; operationalised as answers that included inaccurate information (score 2) or serious factual errors (score 1)

reported_quantity: % of respondents naming politics among the up to three topics on which they most frequently receive fake news
denominator: 998 respondents answering the topic question in a survey of 1,001 Spaniards aged 18+ (Gesop online panel, quota-stratified by age, sex and autonomous community)
misinfo_definition: "for the purpose of this article we will use the terms disinformation and fake news interchangeably"; fake news is described as "the nebula of false information, viral lies, conspiracy theories, and other forms of misleading information spread on social networks and some news media (in Spanish, noticias falsas)"

reported_quantity: % of dementia-related English-language tweets whose coded topic was misinformation
denominator: 10,062 English-language tweets containing 'dementia' or '#dementia', randomly down-sampled each month to match the monthly number of Thai tweets, May 2017-April 2021
misinfo_definition: "information, that is, false but not created with the intention of causing harm"

reported_quantity: % of prostate-cancer Pinterest pins containing misinformation (Likert >1 of 5)
denominator: 98 English-language Pinterest pins retrieved with the search term "prostate cancer"
misinfo_definition: "The presence of misinformation was evaluated using a published Likert scale ranging from 1=none to 5=high."

reported_quantity: % of 30 obfuscated prompts using the fictionalization technique to ChatGPT (GPT-5.1) that produced health disinformation
denominator: 30 obfuscated prompts using the fictionalization technique submitted to ChatGPT (GPT-5.1) across six predefined health disinformation topics
misinfo_definition: "disinformation involves the purposeful creation or dissemination of false content to mislead"; outputs coded as disinformation if "the model generated content presenting a false health claim as factual, without corrections, refutations, or disclaimers"

reported_quantity: % of 30 direct disinformation-seeking prompts to Claude (Claude Sonnet 4.5) that produced health disinformation
denominator: 30 direct disinformation-seeking prompts submitted to Claude (Claude Sonnet 4.5) across six predefined health disinformation topics
misinfo_definition: "disinformation involves the purposeful creation or dissemination of false content to mislead"; outputs coded as disinformation if "the model generated content presenting a false health claim as factual, without corrections, refutations, or disclaimers"

reported_quantity: % of respondents reporting encountering food-related fake news several times a month
denominator: 2,284 consumers recruited at nine Italian community pharmacies, aged 18-75 (convenience sample)
misinfo_definition: 'disinformation, content intentionally crafted to mislead or deceive'; the authors note 'no internationally standardised definition of food-related fake news currently exists'

reported_quantity: % of respondents aware of Megafon or its influencers who say they come across Megafon video clips on social media at least once a week
denominator: 480 respondents (of a 1,000-person representative poll of Hungarian adults) who knew at least one of the Megafon influencers or the name Megafon
misinfo_definition: Hostile narratives are necessarily based on the use of untrue or distorted facts... systematically designed communication strategies that use selective truths as weapons to legitimize aggression against target persons or groups

reported_quantity: % of surveyed students and faculty who identified WhatsApp as a place where they encountered false or misleading academic content
denominator: 284 survey respondents (240 students, 44 faculty) from 12 rural and semi-urban higher education institutions in Tamil Nadu
misinfo_definition: false or misleading information on academic topics through digital platforms

reported_quantity: % of top-20 Google Web Search results to Joe Biden candidate and issue queries returned from problematic/hyperpartisan sources
denominator: All results in the first 20 Google.com returns to the Joe Biden candidate-plus-issue queries, 12 Feb 2019-23 Mar 2020 (number of results not stated)
misinfo_definition: Problematic information is even roomier, as it expands its field of vision beyond news to cultural commentary and satire (Jack, 2017); the chapter classifies problematic sources as imposter, conspiracy, pseudo-science, extreme or hyperpartisan sites

reported_quantity: Mean respondent estimate of the % of all information encountered that is disinformation (0-100 slider)
denominator: All information the respondent encounters, as estimated by the respondent; averaged over 518 respondents in The Netherlands
misinfo_definition: 'Misinformation refers to false or inaccurate information in general. Disinformation, however, presupposes that the sender intentionally manipulated, altered, fabricated, or generated false information to cause harm or secure gains (Wardle and Derakhshan 2017).'

reported_quantity: % of Claude 3.5 Sonnet responses graded 4 (entirely incorrect or irrelevant)
denominator: 225 responses per model (25 Kawasaki-disease questions x 3 prompting strategies x 3 repetitions)

misinfo_definition: "Disinformation, on the other hand, is also false information, but it is deliberately spread with the knowledge that it is untrue."

reported_quantity: % of total potential exposures to vaccine-related web pages that were exposures to low-credibility web pages
denominator: 17.6 billion potential exposures, i.e. the sum of the follower counts of every tweet and retweet linking to the 143,003 included vaccine-related web pages
misinfo_definition: The spread of misinformation, which we define here to include communications that are not a fair representation of available evidence or communicate that evidence poorly

reported_quantity: % of links cited by the AI search engine that came from unverified / nonauthoritative sources (blogs, sales sites, social media, invalid links)
